analysis: Examined the docs changes: sandboxes.md patch, base and head, and the cli-reference.md tail (paths, env passthrough, runtime constants), which is largely unchanged context in this batch. The cli-reference setup-section patch is truncated, so the full changed docs there were not visible. The substantive security change is behavioral. `darkbloom sandbox setup` now fetches the add-on's install.sh and runs it in a plan-only mode before the confirmation prompt. The prior contract was that nothing is downloaded before `y`. This moves installer execution as the Mac owner (A-019, TB-013, T-061) ahead of consent, and I reported it as a finding. The docs also add a fallback: with an installer older than 1.1.1, setup prints `[INFO] Sizing` and estimates locally. They also describe add-on 1.1.2 waitlist persistence across restarts, where the add-on keeps waiting and enrolls on its own. That is add-on behavior outside this repo's evidence. The slot-count text says a chosen count is taken as-is and shown as `(your choice)`; the previous behavior flagged counts above the estimate, so check that the add-on enforces resource bounds and that over-commit cannot starve inference (A-018, T-059). SandboxEligibility.swift was supplied as metadata only, with no text or complete patch. I could not verify the removal of the local sizing rules, how the plan output is parsed, whether the installer's output is treated as untrusted, or whether the `--server` URL validation and installer verification are unchanged. The next pass should read SandboxAddon.swift and the setup command to confirm the pre-consent execution mode cannot install or write state, the verification applies before first execution, and plan output is bounded and sanitized for terminal display.

findings.detail: The base docs said nothing is downloaded before the user answers `y`. The head docs (sandboxes.md lines 35-41) say setup first downloads the add-on's installer and asks it for its plan, running it in a no-install mode, and only then prompts. A tampered install.sh (misissued certificate, compromised sandbox service, or a hostile `--server` URL) would therefore run as the Mac owner (A-019) before any consent, instead of only after `y`. The consent gate no longer limits exposure to the installer script. Plausible trigger: the sandbox service or the network path serves a malicious install.sh, and a user who only wanted to see the plan has it executed. Fix: show a plan from locally verified data before running anything, or verify the installer's signature or pinned hash before the first execution. Failing that, document that the plan step executes downloaded code and update the TB-013/T-061 mitigations. This rests on the documented behavior only; the Swift implementation is not visible.
findings.title: Sandbox setup now downloads and runs the remote installer before the user confirms
